title: Finite-index transfer on evaluated vertical-cohomology bar rows
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative condensed $\mathbf Q$-algebra on the small coherent profinite site with finite jointly surjective covers [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $G$ be a profinite group and $N$ an internal $A$-module with $A$-linear condensed $G$-action [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Fix a nonnegative equivariant injective resolution $a:N[0]\to I^\bullet$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. For every open subgroup $J\subseteq G$, including $G$, define a first-quadrant double complex of abstract $\mathbf Q$-vector spaces
$$D_J^{p,q}=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[\underline J^p],UI^q)(*)=I^q(J^p),\qquad p,q\geq0,$$
where $U$ forgets the action, $*$ is the one-point profinite set, and $A[\underline J^p]$ is the free internal module. Use the evaluation identification and the action-dependent inhomogeneous cofaces of [def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data]: first face uses the $J$-action on $I^q$, interior faces multiply adjacent entries, and last face drops the last entry. Write $d_h$ for their alternating sum and $d_v$ for the resolution differential. They commute [def-sp-double-complex-total]. For each $q\geq0$, put
$$V_{J,q}^p=\ker(d_v:D_J^{p,q}\to D_J^{p,q+1})/\operatorname{im}(d_v:D_J^{p,q-1}\to D_J^{p,q}),\qquad E_J^{p,q}=H^p(V_{J,q}^\bullet,d_h),$$
with $D_J^{p,-1}=0$ and ordinary kernel-modulo-image cohomology [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Restriction of sections along $J^p\hookrightarrow G^p$ gives a cochain map $r_J:V_{G,q}^\bullet\to V_{J,q}^\bullet$.

For every open subgroup $H\subseteq G$ and every $q\geq0$, there exist $\mathbf Q$-linear cochain maps $t_H:V_{H,q}^\bullet\to V_{G,q}^\bullet$ and degree-minus-one maps $h_H$ such that
$$t_Hr_H-[G:H]\,1=d_hh_H+h_Hd_h.$$
These may be chosen simultaneously natural in equivariant chain maps of resolutions, by fixing coset representatives. Consequently the induced maps satisfy
$$H^p(t_H)H^p(r_H)=[G:H]\,1_{E_G^{p,q}}$$
for every $p,q\geq0$. No vanishing of the individual $V_{J,q}^p$ or of their cohomology is asserted. The statement includes $H=G$, trivial $G$ and $N=0$.

proof.text:
For any equivariant internal module $M$, interpret $c\in M(P)$ as a natural generalized section: for a continuous tuple $x:T\to P$, write $c(x)=x^*c\in M(T)$. This is the evaluation convention of [def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data], not a function $P\to M(*)$. Let $B_J^p(M)\subset M(J^{p+1})$ consist of homogeneous sections satisfying $F(ax_0,\ldots,ax_p)=a\cdot F(x_0,\ldots,x_p)$ after every profinite base change; this is one equality over the universal parameter $J^{p+2}$. With alternating deletion differential $\delta$, define
$$\Phi_JF(g_1,\ldots,g_p)=F(1,g_1,g_1g_2,\ldots,g_1\cdots g_p),$$
$$\Psi_Jc(x_0,\ldots,x_p)=x_0\cdot c(x_0^{-1}x_1,\ldots,x_{p-1}^{-1}x_p).$$
Pullback along these continuous coordinate maps and the sectionwise action of [def-sfb-condensed-action-module] define actual $\mathbf Q$-linear maps. In the second formula, simultaneous left multiplication leaves all successive ratios unchanged and multiplies the initial action by $a$; hence $\Psi_Jc$ is homogeneous. Substitution gives $\Phi_J\Psi_J=1$. Conversely the successive ratios of $(x_0,\ldots,x_p)$ reconstruct $(1,x_0^{-1}x_1,\ldots,x_0^{-1}x_p)$, so homogeneity gives $\Psi_J\Phi_JF=F$. These are inverse maps on sections, including $p=0$.

proof.text: Check each coface under these coordinate maps. On the prefix tuple $(1,g_1,g_1g_2,\ldots,g_1\cdots g_{p+1})$, deletion of position zero, followed by homogeneity with $a=g_1$, gives $g_1\cdot\Phi_JF(g_2,\ldots,g_{p+1})$. Deletion of position $i$ for $1\leq i\leq p$ joins the two successive ratios into $g_ig_{i+1}$. Deletion of position $p+1$ drops the last ratio. Thus the alternating deletion differential becomes exactly the action-dependent inhomogeneous differential of [def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data], with the same signs. This also verifies $(dc)(g)=g c-c$ in degree zero. Deleting coordinates twice in the two orders cancels with opposite signs, so $\delta^2=0$. Both coordinate maps commute with restriction $H\hookrightarrow G$ and with any equivariant coefficient map $b:M\to M'$: pullbacks commute with $b$ and $b(x\cdot m)=x\cdot b(m)$. In particular they commute with each equivariant resolution differential $I^q\to I^{q+1}$, giving an isomorphism of double complexes with homogeneous columns. Denote homogeneous restriction by $R$.

proof.text: The right cosets $Hs$ are open and cover compact $G$, so finitely many cover it; since cosets are disjoint there are finitely many in total. Choose a transversal $S$ with representative $1$ for $H$, and put $m=|S|=[G:H]$. Define $\rho(x)=xs^{-1}\in H$ on $Hs$. This is continuous on each open coset, hence continuous on $G$, with $\rho(hx)=h\rho(x)$ and $\rho|_H=1$. Each coset is also closed, since its complement is a union of open cosets. For $a\in G$ let $\pi_a(s)=u$ when $Hsa=Hu$ and put $h_s(a)=sa u^{-1}\in H$. Right multiplication permutes the cosets, so $\pi_a$ is a permutation. For each $s$, $\pi_a(s)$ is locally constant in $a$. The finite intersections of its fibers, over all $s$, give a finite clopen partition of $G$ on each part of which the whole permutation is constant. These constructions use only the topological-group axioms and compactness.

proof.text:
Define $T_M:B_H^p(M)\to M(G^{p+1})$ by
$$(T_Mf)(x_0,\ldots,x_p)=\sum_{s\in S}s^{-1}\cdot f(\rho(sx_0),\ldots,\rho(sx_p)).$$
This expression means the sum of pullbacks along the continuous maps $x\mapsto(\rho(sx_i))_i$, followed by the action of the constant section $s^{-1}$. It is a well-defined $\mathbf Q$-linear operator on sections, without any topology on $M(*)$. Pullback, finite addition and the action commute with every equivariant coefficient map by [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Deletion commutes with applying $\rho(s-)$ to every coordinate, and the constant action is linear. Expanding the two finite sums therefore gives $\delta T_M=T_M\delta$ before imposing homogeneity on the output.

proof.text:
To verify homogeneity, work over the universal parameters $(a,x_0,\ldots,x_p)\in G^{p+2}$. On a clopen piece where $\pi_a$ is a fixed permutation, write $sa=h_s(a)u$ with $u=\pi_a(s)$. Then
$$\rho(sax_i)=h_s(a)\rho(ux_i),\qquad s^{-1}h_s(a)=a u^{-1}.$$
Homogeneity of $f$ is valid for the variable section $h_s(a)$, not just for constant elements of $H$. It changes the $s$-summand at $(ax_i)$ to $a u^{-1}\cdot f((\rho(ux_i))_i)$. Reindex by the permutation $s\mapsto u$ to obtain $(T_Mf)(ax)=a\cdot(T_Mf)(x)$ on that piece. The clopen pieces give a finite jointly surjective cover of the parameter set; the separatedness part of the sheaf condition in [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and the module-sheaf interpretation in [def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data] give the global equality. Thus $T_M$ lands in $B_G^p(M)$. Put $a_s(x)=s^{-1}\rho(sx)\in G$. For homogeneous $F$ on $G$, the same equivariance formula with the constant $s^{-1}$ gives
$$(T_MRF)(x_0,\ldots,x_p)=\sum_{s\in S}F(a_s(x_0),\ldots,a_s(x_p))=:L_MF.$$
Also $a_s(ax)=a a_{\pi_a(s)}(x)$ on each such piece.

proof.text:
Set $K_M^0=0$ and, for $p\geq1$, define
$$(K_M^pF)(x_0,\ldots,x_{p-1})=\sum_{s\in S}\sum_{i=0}^{p-1}(-1)^i F(x_0,\ldots,x_i,a_s(x_i),\ldots,a_s(x_{p-1})).$$
Every summand is pullback of a section along a continuous map $G^p\to G^{p+1}$, so this defines a $\mathbf Q$-linear map into $M(G^p)$. For simultaneous translation by the universal variable $a$, use the same finite clopen partition as in step 5. On each piece the mixed tuple in the summand is $a$ times the tuple with $s$ replaced by $\pi_a(s)$. Homogeneity of $F$ and reindexing $s$ prove homogeneity of the sum on that piece; sheaf separatedness gives it globally. Consequently $K_M^p:B_G^p(M)\to B_G^{p-1}(M)$. Each summand is a pullback, so $K_M$ commutes with every equivariant coefficient map by the evaluation convention of [def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data].

proof.text:
Use the explicit algebraic prism identity of [lem-trf-coefficient-bar-prism-homotopy]. For a fixed $s$, the category with objects the underlying set of $G$ and exactly one arrow between each pair is small in the fixed universe. Set $v=1$, $w=a_s$, use the unique-arrow natural transformation, and constant $\mathbf Z$ coefficients with $t=1$. With $x_j=U_{n-j}$ its prism is the formal signed tuple sum
$$P_n^s[x_0,\ldots,x_n]=\sum_{i=0}^n(-1)^i[x_0,\ldots,x_i,a_s(x_i),\ldots,a_s(x_n)],$$
and the cited face identities give $\partial P^s+P^s\partial=(a_s)_*-1$. This identity also holds as a formal sum of continuous tuple maps: all face identities are coordinate identities before any input tuple is chosen. Namely deletion before the repeated position is the $j<i$ identity; deletion after it is the $j>i+1$ identity; the two joining faces of consecutive prisms agree and cancel; the two outer faces leave $(a_s(x_j))_j$ and $(x_j)_j$, with signs plus and minus. Apply contravariant pullback to these identities and finite addition in the section group. This gives $\delta K_M^{p,s}+K_M^{p+1,s}\delta=(a_s^{\times(p+1)})^*-1$ on $M(G^{p+1})$; no evaluation at ordinary points of $M$ is used. Summing over $s$ gives
$$\delta K_M^p+K_M^{p+1}\delta=L_M-m1=T_MR-m1.$$
For $p=0$, the sole prism evaluates $\delta F$ on $(x_0,a_s(x_0))$, giving $F(a_s(x_0))-F(x_0)$; hence the identity includes degree zero.

proof.text:
Use steps 1–7 with $M=I^q$ in every $q$ and the same $S,\rho$. On the original inhomogeneous double complexes define
$$\tau^{p,q}=\Phi_G^p T_{I^q}^p\Psi_H^p,\qquad k^{p,q}=\Phi_G^{p-1}K_{I^q}^p\Psi_G^p\ (p\geq1),\quad k^{0,q}=0.$$
Restriction becomes $r=\Phi_H R\Psi_G$. The coordinate cochain identities and step 7 give
$$d_h\tau=\tau d_h,\qquad \tau r-m1=d_hk+kd_h.$$
For every equivariant $b:M\to M'$, the action and pullbacks in $T$ commute with $b$, and all pullbacks in $K$ commute with $b$; steps 1–2 give the same for $\Phi,\Psi$. Thus $\tau$ and $k$ commute with each $d_v$ and with every equivariant chain map between resolutions. This uses actual coefficient morphisms, not any exactness of section evaluation. There is no extra sign: $d_v$ here is the commuting column differential, not the signed differential $(-1)^p d_v$ in the totalization of [def-sp-double-complex-total].

proof.text: For any one of the operators $u=\tau,r,k$ just constructed, $d_vu=ud_v$ implies $u(\ker d_v)\subseteq\ker d_v$ and $u(d_vz)=d_v(uz)$. Hence $[z]\mapsto[uz]$ is well defined on the ordinary kernel-modulo-image groups in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], including $q=0$ where the incoming term is zero. This constructs the desired $t_H$ and $h_H$ on every $V_{J,q}$; the same argument gives the horizontal differential there. The identities in step 8 pass to the quotients because sums and composites are evaluated on representatives. Thus $t_H$ is a cochain map and $t_Hr_H-m1=d_hh_H+h_Hd_h$. Naturality passes to the quotients by the identical representative formula, simultaneously for every equivariant chain map of resolutions.

proof.text: If $[z]\in E_G^{p,q}$ is represented by a horizontal cocycle $z\in V_{G,q}^p$, the last identity gives $(t_Hr_H-m1)z=d_h(h_Hz)$ because $d_hz=0$. The difference is a horizontal boundary, proving $H^p(t_H)H^p(r_H)=m1$. For $p=0$, $h_Hz$ lies in the zero negative term, so the same computation is valid. If $H=G$, choose $S=\{1\}$, $\rho=1_G$, so $T=R=1$ and $a_1=1_G$; the prism identity still holds (one may instead choose $h_H=0$). Trivial $G$ is this case. For $N=0$ the construction still applies to any chosen resolution, which need not be the zero complex; no step used nonzero coefficients or any vanishing of its evaluated columns. Only finite sums, restriction, action and representatives in kernels and images were used, so no individual $V_{J,q}^p$ or its cohomology was assumed to vanish.
